# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 3
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
19 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon said, "You have-done with your-servant David my-father great ḥesed, as he-walked before-you in-faithfulness and-in-righteousness and-in-uprightness-of heart with-you. And-you-kept for-him ʾet-this great ḥesed, and-you-gave to-him a-son sitting upon his-throne, as-this day.

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon said, "You have shown great loyal love to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in faithfulness, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart toward you. And you have kept for him this great loyal love and have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon replied, "You showed tremendous faithful love to your servant, my father David, because he lived before you with integrity, righteousness, and an honest heart. And you have continued this great faithful love by giving him a son to sit on his throne today.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** And-now, YHWH my-God, you have-made-king ʾet-your-servant in-place-of David my-father. And-I am a-small youth; I-do-not know going-out or-coming-in.

**LOGOS (formal):** And now, O LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father. But I am a young child; I do not know how to go out or come in.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Now, LORD my God, you have made me king in my father's place. But I am practically a child — I don't know the first thing about leading.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-your-servant is in-the-midst-of your-people whom you-chose, a-great people that cannot be-numbered or-counted from-multitude.

**LOGOS (formal):** Your servant is in the midst of your people whom you have chosen, a great people, too numerous to be numbered or counted.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And here I am, surrounded by your chosen people — a nation so vast it cannot be counted.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** And-give to-your-servant a-hearing heart to-judge ʾet-your-people, to-understand between good and-evil. For who is-able to-judge ʾet-this your-weighty people?"

**LOGOS (formal):** Give your servant therefore a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of yours?"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** So give me a heart that listens — one that can govern your people and tell right from wrong. For who could possibly govern this great people of yours?"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 11
**EMET (literal):** And-God said to-him, "Because you-asked ʾet-this thing, and-you-did-not ask for-yourself many days, and-you-did-not ask for-yourself riches, and-you-did-not ask the-life-of your-enemies, but-you-asked for-yourself understanding to-hear judgment —

**LOGOS (formal):** God said to him, "Because you have asked this, and have not asked for yourself long life, nor asked for yourself riches, nor asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to discern justice —

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** God said, "Because you asked for this — not for a long life, not for wealth, not for your enemies' death, but for discernment in administering justice —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** behold, I-have-done according-to-your-words. Behold, I-have-given to-you a-wise and-understanding heart, so-that like-you there-has-not-been before-you, and-after-you there-shall-not arise like-you.

**LOGOS (formal):** behold, I have done according to your words. Behold, I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so that none like you has been before you, and none like you shall arise after you.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** I am granting your request. I am giving you a mind so wise and perceptive that no one before you has ever had its equal, and no one after you ever will.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 13
**EMET (literal):** And-also what you-did-not ask I-have-given to-you, both riches and-honor, so-that there-shall-not-be a-man like-you among-the-kings all your-days.

**LOGOS (formal):** I have also given you what you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that no king shall compare with you all your days.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And I am also giving you what you did not ask for — wealth and honor beyond any king of your time.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** And-if you-walk in-my-ways, keeping my-statutes and-my-commandments, as David your-father walked, then-I-will-lengthen ʾet-your-days."

**LOGOS (formal):** And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And if you walk in my ways and obey my commands as your father David did, I will also give you a long life."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon awoke, and-behold — a-dream. And-he-came to-Jerusalem and-stood before the-ark-of the-covenant-of the-Lord, and-offered-up burnt-offerings and-made peace-offerings, and-made a-feast for-all his-servants.

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon woke up and realized it had been a dream. He went to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the LORD's covenant, and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then he held a banquet for all his court.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** Then two women, prostitutes, came to the-king, and-stood before-him.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Some time later, two prostitutes came before the king.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was on-the-third day after-my-giving-birth, and-this woman also gave-birth. And-we were together; there-was-no stranger with-us in-the-house — only the-two-of-us in-the-house.

**LOGOS (formal):** On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together; there was no one else with us in the house — only the two of us.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Three days later, she also had a baby. We were alone — no one else was in the house, just the two of us.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 19
**EMET (literal):** And-the-son-of this woman died in-the-night, because she-lay upon-him.

**LOGOS (formal):** This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** During the night, her baby died because she rolled over on him.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 20
**EMET (literal):** And-she-arose in-the-middle-of the-night and-took ʾet-my-son from-beside-me — and-your-maidservant was-asleep — and-laid-him in-her-bosom, and-ʾet-her-dead son she-laid in-my-bosom.

**LOGOS (formal):** She arose at midnight and took my son from beside me while your servant slept, and laid him at her breast, and laid her dead son at my breast.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** She got up in the middle of the night, took my son from beside me while I was sleeping, and put him at her breast. Then she put her dead son next to me.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 22
**EMET (literal):** And-the-other woman said, "No! For my-son is the-living and-your-son is the-dead." And-this-one said, "No! For your-son is the-dead and-my-son is the-living." And-they-spoke before the-king.

**LOGOS (formal):** The other woman said, "No, the living son is mine, and the dead son is yours." The first said, "No, the dead son is yours, and the living son is mine." Thus they spoke before the king.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "That's not true!" the other woman said. "The living baby is mine, and the dead one is yours!" "No!" the first insisted. "The dead one is yours, and the living one is mine!" They argued back and forth in front of the king.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 23
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king said, "This-one says, 'This is my-son, the-living, and-your-son is the-dead,' and-this-one says, 'No! For your-son is the-dead and-my-son is the-living.'"

**LOGOS (formal):** Then the king said, "The one says, 'This is my son that is alive, and your son is dead,' while the other says, 'No, your son is dead, and my son is the living one.'"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The king said, "So. One of you says, 'My son is alive, yours is dead.' The other says, 'No, your son is dead, mine is alive.'"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king said, "Bring to-me a-sword." And-they-brought the-sword before the-king.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword before the king.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then the king said, "Bring me a sword." A sword was brought.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 26
**EMET (literal):** And-the-woman whose-son was the-living said to the-king — for her-compassion burned over her-son — and-she-said, "Please, my-lord, give to-her ʾet-the-living newborn, and-dying do-not kill-him." But-the-other said, "Neither mine nor-yours shall-he-be — divide!"

**LOGOS (formal):** Then the woman whose son was alive said to the king — for her heart yearned for her son — "O my lord, give her the living child, and by no means put him to death." But the other said, "He shall be neither mine nor yours; divide him."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The real mother — her love for her son overwhelmed her — cried out, "Please, my lord! Give her the baby! Don't kill him!" But the other woman said, "Fair enough — neither of us gets him. Cut him in half."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king answered and-said, "Give to-her ʾet-the-living newborn, and-dying do-not kill-him. She is his-mother."

**LOGOS (formal):** Then the king answered and said, "Give the living child to the first woman, and by no means put him to death. She is his mother."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then the king gave his ruling: "Give the baby to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is the mother."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 28
**EMET (literal):** And-all Israel heard ʾet-the-judgment that the-king had-judged, and-they-feared before the-king, for they-saw that the-wisdom-of God was in-him to-do justice.

**LOGOS (formal):** All Israel heard of the judgment that the king had rendered, and they stood in awe of the king, because they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to execute justice.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When all Israel heard about the king's verdict, they were in awe of him. They could see that he had God-given wisdom for doing justice.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
